purpose: Signature-based validation of background rules R1-R3 on all attack captures, R1 audit and manual-audit sample (flow CSVs only).
assumptions: Flow-level evidence only (flow CSVs); "attack-related" is a partial, heuristic ground truth derived without R1-R3. Flows not linked to a signature are unconfirmed, not proven background: kept_attack_share and flagged_attack_share are lower bounds.

Rates are computed on the raw flows of each capture (before the de-duplication and DOS/DDOS caps of flagged_loader.py). R1-R3 are recomputed exactly as in flagged_loader.py (R3: IP pairs of all Benign flows).

bruteforce, web, dns and arp are the signatures of rule_validation.py (its identify() is called unchanged); they restrict attackers/victims to testbed pairs, so R1 is not tested independently for them.

Flood signatures (syn, udp, ackfrag, proto0flood) are direction-agnostic: the sender is the side with more packets (CICFlowMeter orients a flow by its first packet, which can be the victim's reply). Victim hosts = testbed unicast receivers covering >= 80 % of the predicate packets (<= 20); victim endpoints (host:port) are used when <= 20 of them cover >= 80 % of the packets to the victim hosts; attackers = senders covering >= 80 % of the signature packets (<= 50); when no such set exists (e.g. spoofed sources) attacker_victim = signature.

attacker_any adds every flow of an identified attacker (any peer, port or protocol). It is an upper bound: attacks on other ports or hosts are covered, but so is the attacker device's own background traffic.
Flood sources are NOT restricted to the testbed, so R1 is tested independently for the floods: a spoofed or external flood source counts as attack-related and a removal by R1 as a false removal.
proto0flood uses a fixed threshold of 1000 packets per flow; the sensitivity to 100 and 10,000 is reported (heavy_threshold_sensitivity).
mirai_scan targets may be Internet addresses (Mirai scans random addresses), so R1 is tested independently for them; the Mirai capture is scored on the union of proto0flood and mirai_scan.

recon: scanner-initiated flows to testbed hosts are the signature; attacker_victim adds every flow between a scanner and a probed host (any direction/protocol); scanner flows to non-testbed hosts are reported separately.

R1 audit: the external endpoint of a flow is each endpoint outside 192.168.137.0/24 and 205.174.165.0/24; "in Benign" means that every external endpoint of the flow occurs in a Benign flow (address, or the same address:port endpoint in any Benign flow). A spoofed-source candidate is a flow whose external source address is a routable IPv4 address (IPv6, link-local, loopback, multicast and broadcast sources are reported separately), occurs in exactly one flow of the capture, has no backward packet and never occurs in Benign.

DNS extra-answer indicator: UDP/53 flows with an external resolver in which the resolver side sends more packets than the client side (a forged and a genuine answer to one query share one CICFlowMeter flow); retransmitted or multi-part answers can also produce it, hence the Benign baseline.

Audit sample: raw flows of the attack captures (Benign is excluded because the rules are not applied to it); bottom-20 of a seeded hash of (file, row) per class and stratum = a simple random sample per stratum; a flow can be sampled for several strata (column selected_strata).

signatures.bruteforce: rule_validation.py: TCP 22/23 between testbed hosts; attackers = client side (80 % cover, <= 10), victims = server side
signatures.web: rule_validation.py: TCP 80/8080 between testbed hosts; attackers = client side, victims = server side (SQLi, XSS, Uploading, DoS and DDoS HTTP Flood)
signatures.dns: rule_validation.py: rogue DNS responders (testbed hosts other than the gateway answering >= 5 UDP/53 flows)
signatures.arp: rule_validation.py: ARP pseudo-flows 8.6.0.1<->8.0.6.4 plus all flows of the spoofing host (largest ICMP fan-out to testbed hosts)
signatures.syn: TCP, SYN Flag Count >= 1 and >= 0.5 x hi, no payload in either direction, ACK Flag Count <= lo (hi/lo = larger/smaller of forward and backward packets); to a victim (sender = side with more packets)
signatures.udp: UDP, lo = 0, hi >= 10 packets, and >= 100 packets/s per flow or >= 100 such flows to the same receiving host:port starting within one second; to a victim
signatures.ackfrag: (TCP, ACK >= 1, SYN = 0, payload > 0, lo <= 1 or 2 lo <= hi) or (protocol 0, not the ARP pseudo-flow, hi >= 10, lo <= hi/10); to a victim
signatures.proto0flood: protocol 0 (ICMP, GRE, fragments), not the ARP pseudo-flow, >= 1000 packets; to a victim
signatures.mirai_scan: TCP to port 23/2323 from a testbed host (not the gateway) with >= 20 distinct destination addresses on these ports
signatures.recon: TCP/UDP flows from a testbed host (not the gateway) with >= 50 distinct destination ports or >= 30 distinct testbed destination hosts (scanner) to testbed hosts
